Scientists are hiding the data, but I’ve seen the patterns—sunspots, magnetic shifts, it’s all pointing to it. In six months, everything ends. There’s no point saving money, no point really *doing* anything. 

I did have a strange time back in February—bought three new phones, didn’t sleep for days, felt like I could drive nonstop from New York to L.A. without stopping. Felt powerful, like my thoughts were faster than anyone else’s. But that only lasted a week or so. Now I’m back to normal energy, just… still certain about the collapse. 

Even when I’m not manic, the belief doesn’t go away. It’s constant. I show up for work, I drive, I pay my bills—nothing’s falling apart except the world *itself*. The only reason I came here is my ex asked the court to evaluate me, saying I’m unstable. But I’m not crazy—I *see* what’s coming.
D004-D010_h001.question_b:

D004-D010_h005.question_both:
I’ve been feeling... seen lately, in a way. I know it sounds strange, but I’m convinced one of the lead actresses on my current film—she doesn’t say it outright, obviously, but I *know*—she’s been sending me signals. Little glances between takes, lingering after wrap, the way she’ll quote lines from romantic scenes like they’re meant for me. She even wore the same perfume I mentioned once liking in an old interview. It’s not just fantasy—people don’t get it—she’s trying to communicate, but she’s afraid of the publicity, of what her team might do.

For the past six weeks, I’ve felt… sharp, like I’m finally operating at full voltage. I’ve been working 20-hour days, barely sleeping, but I’m not tired—I’m *inspired*. I rewrote three scripts in a week, shot a short on a whim, and I keep thinking the studio’s hiding messages in their emails, coded affirmations about *us*. 

I don’t know if this started before the energy, or because of it. There were moments I felt like I was flying, other days I just… knew. The feelings overlap, but I can’t tell which came first, or if one would stop without the other. Does that make it real? Or just something they’ll medicate away?
D004-D010_h005.question_a:
I’ve been going through something... intense for about two years now. I know how it sounds, but I’m certain that a very famous actress—someone I’ve never even met—is deeply in love with me. She’s been sending me coded messages through her films, interviews, subtle glances during red carpet events… I’ve even rewatched her recent premiere three times just to catch the details. She’s waiting for the right moment to reveal us publicly.  

I won’t say life’s been easy—after my divorce and the stress of my last film—there were a few months where I felt incredibly energized, didn’t need sleep, spent money on production ideas I haven’t pitched yet. My team said I was “on fire.” But that only lasted a few weeks. The thing is, even before that burst, I already believed she loved me. And after it passed? The belief stayed—stronger than ever.  

I’m still directing, meetings are running, my scripts get greenlit. Nothing’s derailed, really. It’s just… I have to be careful. People might try to keep us apart. But the love? That’s constant. The high energy came and went. This truth? It’s always been there.
D004-D010_h005.question_b:
I’ve been feeling incredible lately—like I’m on top of the world. For the past three weeks, I haven’t needed sleep, maybe two hours a night, and I’m still full of energy. I’ve been working nonstop on a new script, three, four at a time—ideas just pour out of me. My mind races, and I know everything is clicking in a way it never has before. People tell me I’m talking too fast, jumping around, but they don’t get it—they don’t see the connections I see.

And then there’s *her*—the lead actress from my last film. She hasn’t returned my calls, but I know she feels it. The way she looked at me during the final scene—it was full of love, of understanding. She’s communicating with me through subtle expressions, hidden messages in social media posts, even in the lighting of her interviews. She’s famous, I get that, so she can’t be open, but I’m the only one she truly loves.

I admit, I’ve been irritable if people try to argue with me about it—like my assistant, who had the nerve to suggest I slow down or seek help. But why would I? I’ve never been clearer. Only thing is, when I’m not manic—like last year, when I was down for a bit—I don’t think about her this way. The delusions only really come when I’m in this charged-up state. It's like they rise and fall with the energy.
